title: What does AMMCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AMMCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AMMCreate initializes an automated market maker for an asset pair by depositing both pool assets. [1]

The creator receives liquidity-provider tokens representing its pool share. Initial amounts establish the starting price, while the trading fee and asset eligibility affect operation. Creating a pool is not evidence that other traders will supply liquidity. Check issuer controls, deposit amounts and special transaction cost before authorizing the initial commitment. [1]

The AMMCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using AMMCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
